events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding. For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of
6-8 feet, sets up to 10 feet along west-facing beaches. For the
Beach Hazards Statement, surf of 4 to 6 feet with sets to 7 feed
and minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, until 1 PM PST this
afternoon. For the High Surf Advisory, until 4 AM PST early this
morning. For the Beach Hazards Statement, from 1 PM PST this
afternoon through Saturday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Numerous roads may be closed. Low lying property
including homes, businesses, and some critical infrastructure
will be inundated. Some shoreline erosion will occur. Dangerous
swimming and surfing conditions and localized beach erosion.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...King Tides peak this morning around 7.5-7.7
feet MLLW. Surf will be falling this morning but remain elevated
into Saturday, especially for west-facing beaches. Sets up to 7
feet. Despite lower surf and waning tides, localized coastal
flooding is still likely through the Saturday morning high
tides.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 6 and 12
inches, mainly above 8000 feet. Winds gusting as high as 50 mph.

* WHERE...Sierra Madre Range.

* WHEN...From 5 PM this afternoon to midnight MST Saturday Night.

* IMPACTS...Outdoor recreation could become dangerous to those caught
unprepared for hazardous winter conditions. Hunters, hikers, and
snowmobilers may become disoriented and lost due to low visibility
in falling and blowing snow. Areas of blowing snow could reduce
visibility and lead to slick road conditions.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Heavy snow and blowing snow expected. Total snow
accumulations between 8 and 16 inches, mainly above 9000 feet in
elevation. Winds gusting as high as 65 mph.

* WHERE...Snowy Range.

* WHEN...From 5 PM this afternoon to midnight MST Saturday Night.

* IMPACTS...Outdoor recreation could become life threatening to those
caught unprepared for severe winter conditions. Hikers and
snowmobilers may easily become disoriented. Frostbite and
hypothermia can develop quickly. Widespread blowing snow could
significantly reduce visibility and lead to dangerous travel
conditions.
